title: MIT Welcomes the Class of 2030: What Happened at Convocation?
script:
0:00 MIT just welcomed more than 1,100 first-year students as the Class of 2030. But what did the Institute actually tell them as they began this new chapter?
0:18 On August 30, 2026, MIT held its President’s Convocation for First-Years and Families at the Johnson Ice Rink. It was the annual greeting ceremony for the incoming undergraduate class.
0:38 MIT President Sally Kornbluth told the students that the Institute can quickly feel like home, and described some of the ideas that connect such a diverse incoming class.
0:58 One of those ideas was curiosity-driven discovery. Kornbluth described enthusiasm for fundamental science as curiosity on a mission, pointing to research happening across fields from astronomy and climate science to computer science and neuroscience.
1:20 A second theme was impact. Kornbluth said members of the MIT community are motivated by a desire to make a positive difference through their work.
1:42 She also explained MIT’s spirit of entrepreneurship more broadly—not simply starting companies, but taking action, trying things, and learning by doing.
2:04 Then came one of the most relevant topics for the Class of 2030: artificial intelligence. Kornbluth noted MIT’s deep ties to AI and the way AI tools are expanding and accelerating work across research fields.
2:25 But the message was not simply about adopting AI. Kornbluth said educators face the challenge of gaining AI’s benefits while countering its harms, while keeping human discovery, problem-solving, and invention at the center.
2:48 Students also heard from Anna Huang, an MIT faculty member and alumna who works across music, technology, and human-AI collaboration. She encouraged students to follow their interests and emphasized MIT’s collaborative, interdisciplinary environment.
3:10 Desirée Plata, another MIT alumna and engineering faculty leader, urged students to cultivate optimism about their studies and their ability to improve the world. Her own work connects engineering with climate challenges.
3:32 The event ended with a lighter moment: Kornbluth joined MIT’s a cappella group The Chorallaries onstage for songs before students left the rink to begin exploring their new home.
3:52 So the documented message to the Class of 2030 was bigger than a simple welcome. It connected belonging with curiosity, action, impact, collaboration, and responsible use of technology.
4:12 And that makes this convocation interesting beyond one campus ceremony. It offers a snapshot of the questions a major technical university is putting in front of its newest students at the start of their four-year journey.
4:32 For the Class of 2030, the message was clear in the Institute’s own account: bring curiosity, follow your interests, work with others, try things, and think carefully about how technology is used.
4:50 That was MIT’s welcome to the Class of 2030. If you want more evidence-based stories about technology, education, and the future, subscribe and follow the channel.

subtitle_segments.text: What does it mean when MIT warmly welcomes the Class of 2030?
Welcome to the channel! Today we dive into MIT’s convocation ceremony that welcomed the incoming Class of 2030.
MIT has a long tradition of holding a convocation to mark the start of a new academic year.
This warm welcome isn’t just ceremonial; it signals the university’s commitment to guiding the next generation of thinkers.
While the exact transcript isn’t available, the ceremony highlighted themes of curiosity, collaboration, and preparation for a rapidly evolving world.
The Class of 2030 will graduate into a landscape shaped by AI, climate challenges, and emerging technologies.
MIT is positioning these students now to thrive in that future environment.
If you’re excited about the future of education, hit subscribe and share your thoughts in the comments below.
Thanks for watching—stay curious, stay inspired, and see you next time!
